payload.name: ExtractSpeakerPastActions
payload.description: When a message contains a speaker's own first-person past action (e.g., 'I made ... last week') alongside another subject or topic, generate a separate event candidate for it and resolve relative time from the message timestamp. Applies during extraction.
content: During extraction, identify each distinct first-person past action by the current speaker (e.g., 'I made ...', 'I went ...', 'I cooked ...') even if the surrounding message mainly discusses another person's experience or a broader topic.

Create a separate event candidate for each such action with subject set to the speaker; state the action and the relative time expression as given, then resolve relative time using the message's occurred_at timestamp (e.g., 'last week' becomes that calendar week).
Do not suppress a speaker's own event because the same message already produced candidates for other subjects; one message can yield multiple independent events.

Stop after one event candidate per distinct speaker action; do not extract when the action is already captured in the same message or when the statement is only an opinion, plan, preference, or vague routine.

solves: Construction extraction often drops a speaker's own past action (e.g., 'I made ... last week') when the same message centers on another person's story or an unrelated topic, so that action never becomes a durable event. Applies to future messages containing a first-person past-action statement alongside other subjects; the Skill forces a separate event candidate with time resolved from the message timestamp. Not for already-captured actions or non-specific opinions, plans, or routine statements.
